title: Fix some issues in the TCP reassemble functions
description:
Fix the issues found when decoding the 5G LI x3 CC PDUs.

The 5G LI x3 CC PDUs are used to report the user data to the LIG for Lawful Interception. The user data can be http or https, and the x3 CC payload can be IP or IPv6. That means, the x3 CC PDUs are user data with 5G LI header added, and then encrypted with TLS. It's possible that many 5G LI x3 CC PDUs encoded in the same TLS application data, and the TLS application data spanning multiple TCP segments. Also, if the user data is https, it can also spanning multiple TCP segments. So, there are two TCP layers, the outer one used to transport the TLS contain all the x3 PDUs, the inner one is the real user data which transport the https data. So, the issue comes: if the two different TCP packets encoded in the same TLS record, and both TCP packets contain several TCP segments, the `msp->first_frame` will be the same value for both two TCP packets. However, TCP use `msp->first_frame` as the key to reassemble the multiple TCP segments in the packet-tcp.c. But, `msp->seq` can never be the same, so, it can be used as the key to do the reassemble.

Here is the capture file for the 5G LI x3 CC PDUs. Without the changes, it can't decrypt these x3 PDUs correctly.
[t8.pcap](/uploads/724c91ba740ec2540cfc511f85cb1320/t8.pcap)
[mdfSvr.key.pem](/uploads/07afd63eb13681ea04f6160fa4225991/mdfSvr.key.pem)

And in the capture file, I found two TCP segments with the same address/port/seq/ack/len, yes, they are totally same, please see the frame 36, the TCP seq is 4255. So, I modified the reassemble.c, because it happened in the real life. It may be a retransmission TCP packets?

notes.body: !6330 has one change that is necessary that affects your file and improves the situation a lot.
Also note that your sample here has TLS inside TLS, which is known to be broken, see [packet-tls.c](epan/dissectors/packet-tls.c#L605-608) and #16109
I can think of some ways to change the fix for #16109 so that TLS inside TLS could work, such as changing the frame_layer number that used to be there with a count of the number of layers of TLS.
Please move this into a different merge request. I'm not sure that we want to change this; TCP retransmission detection should normally prevent this from happening, and the error message is useful.

It's true that when due to encapsulation, multiple TCP segments appear in the same frame, it's possible that more than one multisegment PDU can begin in the same frame, so `msp->first_frame` is not a unique key.

Changing it to `msp->seq` does bring some risk, since TCP sequence numbers wrap around more quickly than the frame number, since they're based on the number of bytes. Possibly a more ideal solution is to generate a unique ID for each msp on a given 5 tuple.

OTOH, there already are some known issues for when TCP sequence numbers wraparound - #10503 - so I'm not sure that this changes makes things worse.
Also, [packet-tcp.h](epan/dissectors/packet-tcp.h#L177) should be changed if `seq` is used as the key instead of `first_frame`, to keep the comments accurate.

Hi John, 

Thanks for the update. I just provide a possible fix for the reassemble issue I met. It may cause other issues like you said, So, maybe we should raise a bug to involve more dev to discuss and solve it? Thus, I will close this merge request.

OK. There are two issues affecting your capture, both of which need to be fixed. One issue is that TLS over TLS is broken, because the layer numbers are not stable from the first pass to later passes - #17977 

A second issue is the one you mention here, that using the first frame of a multisegment PDU for the reassembly ID doesn't work when there's more than one such msp in the frame. Note that there's already a workaround for that in `packet-tls.c` because more than one TLS segment in a frame is more common. However, there's several approaches to go for that. Filing a new bug for that separate issue is a good idea.

One reason why using just the sequence number is not a great idea is that there's a possibility of reused connections with the same ports, and the sequence number might be reused. There's a higher likelihood of that with relative sequence numbers enabled, since the relative sequence number is the value used within `desegment_tcp` when that is enabled. The tcp reassembly tables use the addresses and ports, and don't differentiate between connections (even though the multisegment pdu trees are per connection / flow.)

TLS uses a few bits from the sequence number XORed with the frame number, which generally works though there is a slight chance of collision.

The most correction solution is to use the sequence number but change the reassembly table functions to only match for the given flow.
